_about: Every public-domain C. H. Spurgeon (1834-1892) text the Word Hoard holds. CCEL ThML (clean) for the sermons, 63 volumes (1855-1917, the New Park Street and Metropolitan Tabernacle Pulpit as CCEL issues them), and seven other CCEL works. The Treasury of David is NOT taken from CCEL: CCEL's treasury1-6 XML files are stubs (about 4 KB of text each; the psalms live on separate web pages), so it is held as Internet Archive OCR of the seven-volume American printing (Funk & Wagnalls, 1882-1886), assembled from two scan series, each volume identified by the psalm range on its title page. Raw and unconverted. Added 2026-10-10 (round 17, from the Classical reading-lists thread's pickups): Lectures to My Students (first and second series, 1875-77; the third, The Art of Illustration, from Gutenberg), The Soul-Winner (1895), Around the Wicket Gate, Talks to Farmers and Gleanings among the Sheaves. John Ploughman's Talk was not found in a pre-1930 scan or on Gutenberg in this round's search. Extended 2026-10-28 by lane A at Adam's request (his Logos author list): the four-volume Autobiography compiled from his diary and letters by his wife and secretary (1897-1900), The Saint and His Saviour, Feathers for Arrows, John Ploughman's Talk and Pictures, The Salt-Cellars, My Sermon Notes (four volumes), Eccentric Preachers, The Gospel of the Kingdom, the sermon collections he issued as books (Types and Emblems, Trumpet Calls, The Present Truth, Storm Signals, Farm Sermons, Messages to the Multitude and others; some of these sermons also stand in the Metropolitan Tabernacle Pulpit), his Prayers (1905) and his Letters (1923). Every printing dated before 1930.
